$comment: The layout system the console and the desktop panel share. Both repos carry this file; each repo's gate asserts its own stylesheet uses these numbers AND that this file's sha256 matches the literal recorded in the other repo's test. Change it in both repos or neither.

ground.$comment: The surface every page sits ON, which both draw (the fifty-fourth list). ONE colour per theme — no gradient, because a wash behind a page is decoration carrying no information, and rule 17 refuses it. Measured: the panel carried three decorative gradients behind a fixed overlay plus a fourth on its canvas, in six hand-written colours, while the console painted one.

palette.$comment: The greys, and the two rules about them (the fifty-sixth list). `ink` and `muted` were already identical on both surfaces; the THIRD grey was not — `#696a74` on the console and `#6f707a` on the panel, six apart on one channel and identical on the others, two names for a colour the eye cannot tell from the other. A palette is: ink, muted, faint, one accent, and the semantic four. Anything else is a decision that has to be made in the open.

space.$comment: The rhythm, and the two ways a number that is not on it can still be right (the fifty-ninth list). A rhythm is a scale: **2/4/6/8/10/12/14/16/24** — the steps BOTH surfaces declare; the console has a 32 step the panel does not, and the contract records the shared ladder rather than the union, because a step one surface cannot reach is not a rhythm they share. A painting value OFF it is a nudge UNLESS it measures something else: a CONTROL's height (5 + 5 + an 18 px line box = 28) or the padding inside a FIXED target (1 px inside a 24 px box). Those are named tokens, so an editor who changes a line-height cannot silently change a control's height.

leading.$comment: Line-height, as THREE ratios rather than eight (the sixtieth list). Measured before: the console declared `1` (8x), `1.45` (7x), `1.5` (9x), `1.4` (3x), `1.2` (2x), `1.6`, `1.55` and `0`; the panel `1` (10x), `1.5` (6x), `1.55` (4x), `1.6` (3x), `1.45` (2x) and `1.3` — and on ONE rendered page the same 13 px text painted 19.5 px, 16.5 px and `normal`. A reader cannot see .05 of a ratio, so it was never a choice. `mark` is 1 and means a GLYPH IN A BOX (a dot, a chevron, a button's label inside a fixed control); a sentence may not take it.

measure.$comment: How wide a line of PROSE runs (the sixty-first list). Measured before: the panel's `.archive-row-item` ran to 103 characters and `.connect-where` to 109 while Memory's entries stopped at 66 and the console's prose at 46 — the same product asking a reader to move their eye 1,120 px on one page and 517 on another. A measure is not a taste: 66ch is where the block that already reads well sits, and it is inside the 45-75 band a line is followed back along. A CODE SNIPPET IS EXEMPT — scanned token by token, and wrapping it would break copy-paste — so this is a TOKEN a rule opts into, never a blanket.

hairline.$comment: The one family of SEPARATING lines, and the rule about state marks (the fifty-seventh list). A hairline separates two regions and takes `line`; a STATE MARK declares a state and takes its own colour (a pill's edge is its ink, so greyscale keeps its shape and its word). Measured before: the panel had THREE names for the first family — `--line` and `--chrome-line` were the same `rgba(0,0,0,.08)` written twice, and `--glass-hairline` was a COOL `rgba(24,32,54,.07)` for the same job on the same page.

head.$comment: The page's ONE head (the sixty-second list). Its height is its CONTENTS — the pages measured 68/68/33 px because one carries tabs and two carry a subtitle — so `height` is not a number. What IS recorded: the gap, the alignment, the subtitle SLOT (the second line of the title's block, `.page-sub`), and the rule that a page has ONE head — anything under it is a card.

cardTitle.$comment: The card's TITLE, which both surfaces draw (the fifty-third list). Measured before: the panel's card header drew `h2` at 14/600 and the console's drew `<strong>` at 13/600 — the same visual role, two elements at two sizes, and on the console the element that LOOKED like the title was not one. `level` is the section above it (`section.h2` is 17), so the pair is a two-step ladder rather than two opinions.

elevation.$comment: The three LEVELS a shadow can mean, and which atoms may carry one (the fifty-fifth list). `flat` is a card ON the page — a hairline and a tint, no shadow. `pane` is a surface ABOVE it (a drawer, a modal, a popover) and is the only thing that floats. `raised` is a control lifted inside a pane (a segmented switch's active arm), a 1-2 px lift. Measured before: the panel's card carried a four-layer `--glass-shadow` while the console's carried `none`, so a card was two objects on the two surfaces.

radius.$comment: The corner scale, and WHAT EACH STEP IS FOR (the fifty-eighth list). The rule is not the count but the MEANING: a page nests card -> row -> control -> mark, and each is one step; an overlay is drawn LARGER than the pane it covers, which is why its steps are bigger. Measured: `--radius-lg: 20px` is painted on NO page a person browses — the console uses it inside three overlays and the panel on one dialog — so the largest step is an OVERLAY step and is recorded as one. `row` (10) was the step neither side assigned: the panel's own comment called it "cards inside a pane" while painting it on `.btn` and `.tab`, and the console paints it on `.fleet-row` and `.tool-list`. A 40 px TARGET and a 24 px control are the same proportion, so they cannot share one value: `target` is its own step.

rail.$comment: Each surface's first column. The CONSOLE collapses at `tablet` (767): below it the rail becomes the top bar, so the page's left is 0 — measured at 380/480/639. The PANEL never collapses: it is a device app in a window, and its rail is the page's first column at every width. The widths are recorded rather than equalized; the COLLAPSE is a rule, not a habit.

section.$comment: The levels UNDER a page title (the forty-ninth list). A page has one title and the blocks below it are a LEVEL, not a size chosen per page: `h2` is a section, `h3` is the thing inside one, `eyebrow` is the small uppercase label above a block. Measured before: an h2 was 22, 17, 14 or 10 px depending on the page.

empty.$comment: The EMPTY state's atom, which both surfaces draw (the forty-sixth list). A page with nothing to list shows one card, on the page's own grid: the card's corner and padding, start-aligned text, no shadow, and the full width of the page's column. It is NOT a dialog — a 20px corner, a drop shadow and centred text on a 1120px column is a modal drawn where a page's empty state belongs.

loading.$comment: The LOADING state's atom, which both surfaces draw (the forty-seventh list). A read that has not answered reserves the SHAPE of what it will draw: a card-sized skeleton row per item, with the read's own label in a live region. It is NOT a word in a result line: a loading state is not a result, and the count line is drawn only when it has a count.

failed.$comment: The FAILED state's atom, which both surfaces draw (the forty-eighth list). A failure is a NOTICE: the page's card grammar with the alarm's tint, its words in INK (the sentence is the message; the tint is the alarm), one Retry, and ONE live region — a second region saying the same failure in other words is two announcements.

motion.$comment: Rule 18's mechanism, recorded once for both surfaces (the fifty-second list). REDUCED MOTION IS A BLANKET: every transition and animation is capped at 0.01ms under `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, because a NAMED LIST cannot cover a rule added later — measured, the panel still moved 4 elements at 0.2s under reduce while the console moved 0. The named list stays for the second half: an animation whose state must also stop (`animation: none`). `0.01ms` rather than `0s` so a `transitionend` listener still fires.
